final_proof:
Let \(v_p:\mathbb Q_p^\times\to\mathbb Z\) be the normalized \(p\)-adic valuation, so that \(v_p(p)=1\) and \(|x|_p=p^{-v_p(x)}\) for \(x\ne0\), while \(|0|_p=0\). Recall that
\[
\mathbb Z_p=\{x\in\mathbb Q_p:|x|_p\le1\}.
\]
First, \(\mathbb Z_p\) is a commutative ring with identity. It contains \(0\) and \(1\); if \(x,y\in\mathbb Z_p\), then the ultrametric inequality gives
\[
|x-y|_p\le\max\{|x|_p,|y|_p\}\le1,
\]
and multiplicativity gives \(|xy|_p=|x|_p|y|_p\le1\). Also \(p\in\mathbb Z_p\), since \(|p|_p=p^{-1}\le1\), so \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is an ideal of \(\mathbb Z_p\).

We claim that
\[
p\mathbb Z_p=\{x\in\mathbb Z_p:|x|_p<1\}.
\]
Indeed, if \(x=pz\) with \(z\in\mathbb Z_p\), then
\[
|x|_p=|p|_p|z|_p\le p^{-1}<1.
\]
Conversely, suppose \(x\in\mathbb Z_p\) and \(|x|_p<1\). If \(x=0\), then \(x=p\cdot0\in p\mathbb Z_p\). If \(x\ne0\), the value group of the normalized \(p\)-adic norm is \(p^{\mathbb Z}\). Thus \(|x|_p<1\) implies \(v_p(x)\ge1\), and consequently
\[
|x/p|_p=p|x|_p=p^{1-v_p(x)}\le1.
\]
Hence \(x/p\in\mathbb Z_p\), so \(x=p(x/p)\in p\mathbb Z_p\). This proves the claim. In particular, \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is proper, since every element of it has norm less than \(1\), whereas \(|1|_p=1\).

Now let \(x\in\mathbb Z_p\setminus p\mathbb Z_p\). By the displayed characterization, \(|x|_p\not<1\). Since \(x\in\mathbb Z_p\), it follows that \(|x|_p=1\). Thus \(x\ne0\), and
\[
|x^{-1}|_p=|x|_p^{-1}=1.
\]
Therefore \(x^{-1}\in\mathbb Z_p\), so \(x\) is a unit of \(\mathbb Z_p\). Hence every element outside \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is a unit.

A proper ideal cannot contain a unit, because an ideal containing a unit \(u\) also contains \(uu^{-1}=1\) and is therefore the whole ring. Consequently, if \(I\) is any proper ideal of \(\mathbb Z_p\), then every element of \(I\) belongs to \(p\mathbb Z_p\); hence \(I\subseteq p\mathbb Z_p\).

Since \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is itself proper, this proves that it is maximal: any proper ideal containing \(p\mathbb Z_p\) must also be contained in it. Moreover, if \(M\) is any maximal ideal of \(\mathbb Z_p\), then \(M\) is proper, so \(M\subseteq p\mathbb Z_p\); maximality of \(M\) and properness of \(p\mathbb Z_p\) force \(M=p\mathbb Z_p\). Thus \(p\mathbb Z_p\) is the unique maximal ideal of \(\mathbb Z_p\). By definition, a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal is local. Therefore \(\mathbb Z_p\) is a local ring and its unique maximal ideal is \(p\mathbb Z_p\), proving (a) and (b).
